task: Continuous physical wheel docking, RGB-D detection, learned arm grasp/lift/hold/set-down/release
navigation: Local encoder-seeded 2-D lidar scan-to-map SLAM with direct dock controller on an unobstructed lane; not a combined obstacle-navigation benchmark
arm_ik_base_pose_source: Ideal simulated base pose and joint proprioception; object target comes only from RGB-D pixels

camera_detection.assumptions: Known upright 36 mm orange cube; visible top surface; calibrated RGB-D camera.

brake: Encoder-position feedback through effort-bounded wheel velocity motors; no world constraint

final_controller.note: Learned size-conditioned grasp; scripted stages and numerical IK; simulated upright cubes only

limitations: Heavy 80 kg chassis was selected for stability and differs from the standalone 3 kg navigation robot.
Straight docking lane only; the full navigation benchmark and combined manipulation are distinct tests.
Stationary calibrated external RGB-D camera and known upright cube size.
Arm IK uses ideal simulated base pose and joint proprioception, while base docking is controlled from the lidar-map estimate.
No learned whole-body locomotion policy or dynamic manipulation while driving.
